“I was like, sure, let them go off into the sunset together, self-exile, prevent Telemachus from being tainted by the murder of everybody, like totally fine,” she says.
Christensen, meanwhile, found the ending to be a let down. For one, Damon’s Odysseus doesn’t kill all the suitors – he spares them. This merciful Odysseus felt unfamiliar to Christensen.

“What frustrates me is that it set him up to be merciful at the end. The men kneel down and he’s just like, ‘OK, I’m in exile now. Let’s go.’ Which, it’s just weird. What I wanted to happen, because it would have been more true to the poem, is for him to kill the kneeling men,” Christensen says.
He also likes the poem’s original ending for two reasons.
“It’s a complex political story about how we continue to live with people who’ve who’ve murdered our loved ones,” he says.
He also thinks it’s interesting that a poem about remembering ends with a mass forgetting: “It’s basically saying all of this is too dangerous.”
Odysseus’ act of mercy also underlines the difference in characterization between book and movie.

“Homer’s Odysseus is more realistic and complicated because it forces us to think about things aren’t black and white. Nolan’s Odysseus is more aspirational, which is ultimately more comforting because we all want the hero to be a good guy,” he says.
Zeus’ Law or the Golden Rule?
“The Odyssey” movie is hung up Zeus’ law, defined as the idea that anyone could be a god in disguise, so you must be welcoming. This is how the suitors get away with camping out at Ithaca for years.

But the trust and respect goes both ways. So, the Greek soldiers break with Zeus’ law when they hide inside the horse, meant to be a gift for the city, and sack Troy. Odysseus thinks this rupture has led to the breakdown of civilization.
Christensen says he thought it was “strange” that Zeus’ law came down to “do unto others and you would have them to unto you.”
“I guess it would be too hard to explain that you hospitality in the ancient world isn’t the same as like the Christian ideal,” Christensen says.
Circe — and Samantha Morton — Was the Highlight
Of all of Odysseus’ adventures, one stood out to the classicists.
“The scene that shows the promise of remaking Greek myth in film the most was the Circe scene,” Christensen says.

On their way home, Odysseus and his men visit Circe’s (Samantha Morton) island, where she lives alone — save for a few exotic animals. Turns out those animals, like lions and deer, are men whom she has transformed. Odysseus’ men are next.
After ravenously eating her stew, Odysseus’ men start to transform into pigs.

Morton’s turn as the character has been acclaimed. In a ranking of all of the performances in “The Odyssey,” Variety placed Morton at No. 1. She adds something new to the role, implying that she’s a victim of sexual assault in the past. “You’re giving her some motivation for her activity but it wasn’t too heavy,” Christensen says.
Austin, who went to see the movie in London with another classicist friend, said they were both “really grossed out” by the Circe scene, but loved it.
“We were having a lot of really similar reactions. We were a little bit vocal. I hope we did not annoy the people there, but we were really impressed,” she says.
Christensen also thought the siren scene was “really great.” Odysseus, in the movie, describes the song of the sirens as “the song of all the promises I failed to keep.”
“I found that type of internal deliberation and rumination really interesting,” Christensen says.

He adds that “most of the action scenes were just really well done. The sacking of Troy, the Trojan horse was imaginative. I think really effective. So those things really, really worked for me,” he says.

title: Colson Whitehead Says He Doesn’t Write Every Day: ‘Real Imposition on My Lifestyle, Frankly’
summary: Two-time Pulitzer winner Colson Whitehead opens up about his writing process and his new novel “Cool Machine” on “Glass Half Full.”
story: One of the core pieces of creative writing advice is rebuffed by bestselling novelist and two-time Pulitzer winner Colson Whitehead.
“People say, ‘Write every day.’ That seems like a real imposition on my lifestyle, frankly,” Whitehead told Craig Melvin for the July 21 episode of “Glass Half Full.”
“Sometimes I’m not feeling it. Sometimes it’s like, Thanksgiving, and you have to be present for your family or whatever. So that’s a lost week,” he said as Craig laughed.
Instead, Whitehead described his goal as hitting a certain number of pages a week.

“If I can do like six pages a week: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday and Sunday. That’s an accumulation. After a month you have like 20 something (pages), and after 10 months, you got, you know, 240,” he said.
Whitehead added that he feels “lucky” to work from home, where his writing routine can be a little more flexible — and unconventional.
“I can write a page, take a nap, do some spontaneous weeping, get back to work,” he said.
“That’s quite the process,” Craig said, before asking about Whitehead’s hobbies outside of work.

“When I’m not working, I’m really not working at all,” Whitehead said. “I cook a lot. I have a smoker, so a big slab of ribs, a brisket, that’s always fun in the summer. I’ll goof off and play video games. Stare off into space. Think about my regrets. And then when I’m ready to work, I’ll go back to work.”
He added that this hobbies inspire his work and help “clear my head” for what’s next.
Whitehead’s latest project, “Cool Machine,” hit shelves July 21. It’s the final volume in his “Harlem Trilogy,” which also contains bestsellers “Harlem Shuffle” and “Crook Manifesto.”
Although Whitehead told Craig that his newest book is always his favorite, “Cool Machine” still stands apart. The novel feels “closest” to who he is, he said.
“I really think I did what I set out to do,” Whitehead said. “I’m pretty proud of it.”
As for what’s next?
“My next work — my next book is enough of a stretch and a challenge,” Whitehead said.

“It’s a novel. It takes place in the 19-teens, and it’s not something I’ve done before. So the challenge of, ‘What am I doing? Why did I take this on?’ is exciting,” he added. “The characters are coming together.”

title: Robert Irwin Gets Emotional Helping Grieving ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’ Contestant After Mother’s Death
summary: Robert Irwin shared a special moment with a contestant during the latest episode of “Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro” when the two bonded over losing one of their parents at a young age.
story: Robert Irwin shared a special moment with a contestant during the latest episode of “Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro” when the two bonded over losing one of their parents at a young age.

In the second episode of the “Dancing With the Stars” spinoff, which aired July 20, the 14 remaining contestants were paired up and tasked with choreographing a dance that told the story of a significant moment in their lives. Dancer Allen Genkin, 36, decided to portray the absence he has felt since his mother died.

Genkin practiced the choreography with partner Adele Zaikman, explaining to her that for one particular move he wanted her to represent his mother being an angel looking over him. After rehearsals, Genkin became emotional and confided in Irwin, whose father Steve Irwin died when he was just 2 years old, and the two had a poignant conversation about grief.

“I wanted to visit Allen today because I know he’s telling a very important story, and a story that’s hard to tell. I want to see if I can help him through,” Robert Irwin, who hosts the competition series, explained in a voiceover.
While speaking with Genkin about the challenge, Robert Irwin said, “This week is heavy. But I feel like, particularly for you, it’s an important story.”
Genkin then shared that his mother, whom he described as his “best friend,” died when he was 15.

“You know, 20 years have gone by. They say time heals all wounds, but it really doesn’t,” he told Robert Irwin, who shook his head and agreed with Genkin. “And the only way I could really do it justice is to really showcase it through art, and that’s what I want to do.”
Robert Irwin said he could relate to Genkin because he also confronted the pain of losing a parent through dance.

“I understand what it’s like to lose someone. When I did ‘Dancing With the Stars,’ I was given this opportunity to do a dedication dance to my mom. As soon as that music stopped, my mom joined me on stage, and I completely broke down,” he recalled, referring to the Season 34 “Dedication Night” episode and the emotional embrace he shared with mom Terri Irwin.

Robert Irwin, who also performed a tribute to older sister Bindi Irwin in another episode and went on to win the season, continued, “It’s like you’re facing something for the first time in your life that you’ve never had the strength to face. But movement and dance, that is the thing that gives you the ability to face that.”
Genkin took the advice to heart and said he would use the dance as a chance to reconnect with his late mother.
“I think this is going to be the closest I’ve been to her since,” he said.
Tears filled Genkin and Robert Irwin’s eyes before the two hugged. “I’ll be right there with you, man,” Robert Irwin sweetly told him.
The 22-year-old zookeeper and conservationist has opened up before about grieving his dad, who died in September 2006 after a stingray attack.
During an interview on CNN’s “All There Is with Anderson Cooper” podcast in March, Robert Irwin revealed he still talks to his dad and feels his presence.

“I’m always closest to dad when I’m in the middle of nowhere, you know, when I’m out in the bush,” he shared. “There are absolutely moments where I’ll be hit with this sense of — it’s warmth, it’s like something kind of wraps around me.”
In those moments, he often asks his dad, “How do I go forward?”
Although he doesn’t hear an answer, he said he feels a “resolution.”

“There are these checkpoints that I find throughout life where you’re kind of going through the motions and then sometimes something will just hit you, and you need to just step away,” he said. “You need to download and you need to let loose. You need to go, ‘OK, I need to refocus on what is my grief journey.”

title: Lionel Messi Speaks Out After Argentina Loses World Cup: ‘The Pain Is Immense’
summary: Lionel Messi reflected on his 2026 World Cup journey, including Argentina’s wins and loss against Spain.
story: After a heartbreaking loss against Spain during the World Cup final, Lionel Messi is forever grateful for how far he and Team Argentina made it.
On July 19, Spain beat the reigning champs 1-0 in extra time, ending an incredible and historic World Cup run for the 39-year-old soccer legend.
Reflecting on the painful defeat in a July 20 Instagram post, Messi shared a photo of himself wearing his second place medal while on the pitch.
“El dolor es muy grande y va a costar que cierre esta herida,” he wrote in Spanish, which translates to, “The pain is immense and this wound will take time to heal.”

“But I will also hold onto all the good memories... The matches where we turned it around and gave it our all, moments that will remain in our memories forever, the support from our entire country which, with this group’s hard work and effort, brought us back among the best in the world,” he continued.
The one-time World Cup champ did note that right now, at this moment, “It is hard to fully appreciate” all that he and the team accomplished during the tournament.

“But this group reached two consecutive World Cup finals,” he wrote. “Thank you from the bottom of my heart for every greeting and every message. Once again, we managed to unite as a country and be together, sharing the immense pride of being Argentinian.”
He concluded his post by taking a moment to send a message to the new World Cup champs.
“I also want to congratulate Spain on winning the championship,” he wrote.
His comments section was filled with fans and brands thanking him for everything he’s contributed to the sport and his country. Many also called him the greatest of all time.

While this may be Messi’s final World Cup, the soccer star has participated in a total of six. He is, however, not retiring. The forward is currently a captain for Major League Soccer club Inter Miami. In 2025, he signed a contract with the team that extends through the 2028 MLS season.
The eight-time Ballon d’Or winner will have a short break as Inter Miami’s next match is July 22. Though, at this time, there is no confirmation if he will be playing in the game.

title: Does ‘The Odyssey’ Have an End Credits Scene?
summary: Does The Odyssey have an end credits scene? Here’s what to know about the ending of The Odyssey and what happens next.
story: Warning: This contains spoilers for the end of “The Odyssey.”
For nearly three hours, “The Odyssey” takes theatergoers on an epic journey.

The highly anticipated film was a hit at the box office in its first weekend of release, with the tale of Odysseus (Matt Damon) from one of the most celebrated works of literature in world history captivating movie fans to the tune of $264.1 million in ticket sales worldwide.

Packed with Hollywood stars like Damon, Anne Hathaway, Zendaya, Tom Holland, Lupita Nyong’o, Charlize Theron and Robert Pattinson, the movie has brought director Christopher Nolan’s vision of the ancient Greek epic to life and debuted to rave reviews.
“For me to take on Greek mythology on a big modern cinematic canvas is something that hasn’t been done,” Nolan told Kaylee Hartung on TODAY July 17.

A staple of many modern blockbusters has been an extra post-credits scene rewarding moviegoers who stick around until the absolute end. They have become a fixture in superhero and animated movies, popping up in “Masters of the Universe,” “Superman,” “The Fantastic Four: First Steps” and “Moana 2” among recent big films.
But when the credits roll on the nearly three-hour long “Odyssey,” is there one more scene at the end? Here’s what to know.
Is There a Post-Credits Scene at the End of ‘The Odyssey’?

No, once the swords-and-sandals epic has wrapped up after its 172-minute run time, that’s the end. There’s no secret scenes of Odysseus (Matt Damon) and his wife Penelope (Anne Hathaway) starting a new life in Los Angeles or anything.
Director Christopher Nolan had certainly done enough without needing any extra scenes, considering “The Odyssey” took three painstaking months to shoot all on 70-millimeter IMAX film.

“I definitely hit the limits of my own stamina and everybody’s stamina, I think. I mean, it’s ‘The Odyssey,’ of course it should be difficult,” he said on TODAY. “We’re not doing the job right making a film of ‘The Odyssey’ if it doesn’t seem difficult.”
So What Does Happen at the End of ‘The Odyssey’?
You would think there doesn’t need to be a spoiler alert for a story that was composed more than 2,000 years ago, but Nolan did put his own twist on the ending that differs from Homer’s epic poem.

In Nolan’s version, Odysseus and Penelope leave their son Telemachus (Tom Holland) behind and sail west toward the setting sun (probably not to Los Angeles). Odysseus is exiled, but he is with his beloved wife, who dreamed they would sail off together when news of the Trojan War first broke out.

In Homer’s version, the gods have much more of a say in how the story ends. Odysseus and Telemachus are about to battle all the angry families of Penelope’s suitors in Ithaca after Odysseus murdered all the wannabe husbands. However, the gods intervene.
“Zeus hurls a thunderbolt, and Athena makes them swear a truce,” Celsiana Warwick, assistant professor in the University of Iowa Department of Classics, tells TODAY.com.
Odysseus also isn’t done appeasing the gods, as the seer Tiresias tells Odysseus earlier in the poem that he must make a sacrifice to Poseidon in order to lift Poseidon’s curse on him.

title: ‘The Odyssey’ Ending Explained: Christopher Nolan’s Movie Rewrites the Poem in This 1 Way
summary: What happens at the end of the Odyssey? What happens next for Odysseus? This is Christopher Nolan’s twist and what the myth says.
story: Warning: This contains spoilers for the end of “The Odyssey.”
You might have read “The Odyssey” before, but Christopher Nolan’s rendering of the epic poem, part of the Homeric cycle, offers up a brand new experience.

That’s especially true of the ending. Nolan reimagines what happens when Odysseus, played by Matt Damon, returns to Ithaca after 10 years fighting in the Trojan War and another 10 years trying to return to his kingdom.
Here’s what to know about Nolan’s twist on the ending of “The Odyssey,” how the real poem ends and the surprising, and unofficial, continuation of Odysseus’ story.
What Happens at the End of Christopher Nolan’s ‘The Odyssey’?
Nolan’s “Odyssey” will be unfamiliar for those who read the epic poem.
It’s a bittersweet ending for Odysseus and his wife, Penelope (Anne Hathaway). After murdering the suitors who had been trying to court her, Odysseus is exiled from Ithaca.

He and Penelope leave their son Telemachus (Tom Holland) behind and sail west toward the setting sun, which is what Penelope dreamed they’d do when news of the Trojan War first broke out. Yes, he’s exiled — but at least they’re together.

Odysseus also reckons with the dire outlook for civilization at large and his role in it. Odysseus feels that the invasion of Troy broke “Zeus’ law,” cited throughout the movie — the code of conduct that says you should treat hosts and guests well, because anyone could be a god. The Trojan Horse, an act of war disguised as a gift, was a breach of the code.

Odysseus feels that this has led to the collapse of civilization. The “sea people,” spoken of throughout the movie with fear, are the returning Greek soldiers sacking towns, and spreading the violence that started in Troy.
He references the idea of oral history, which is how “The Odyssey” and its companion story “The Iliad” began. When people can no longer read, they will tell the stories of Troy in poems.

Scholar Joel Christensen, editor of “The Oxford Critical Guide to Homer’s Odyssey,” points out that Damon’s Odysseus does something Homer’s Odysseus doesn’t: Spares some of the suitors’ lives. He says Damon’s Odysseus is more of a “good guy” than the original.
“What I wanted to happen because it would have been more true to the poem is for him to kill the kneeling men,” Christensen says.
What Happens at the End of Homer’s ‘The Odyssey’?
“The ending of ‘The Odyssey’ is kind of strange,” Celsiana Warwick, assistant professor in the University of Iowa Department of Classics, tells TODAY.com.
The Hollywood version of the story might end with Penelope and Odysseus’ reunion. But that would have been “unsatisfying” to an ancient audience, Warwick says.

Instead, Odysseus has to face consequences for murdering all of the suitors, which compromise an elite swath of Ancient Greece’s population. The families of the suitors swarm Ithaca, wanting to get revenge on Odysseus and Telemachus. They’re about to rush into battle when the gods intervene. “Zeus hurls a thunderbolt, and Athena makes them swear a truce,” Warwick says.
Warwick adds that the ending speaks to an element of Greek culture during the archaic period “where blood feuds between aristocratic families could get way out of hand.”
“That’s something that would have been of great interest to an ancient audience, perhaps not so much to a modern audience,” she says.

Odysseus’ wandering continues, too, though his departure from Ithaca is not actually depicted in “The Odyssey.” Earlier on in the poem, the seer Tiresias tells Odysseus what he must do after killing the suitors.

In order to lift Poseidon’s curse, Odyssey has to take an oar and go on a journey until he finds men who don’t recognize it and know nothing of the sea. There, he will make a sacrifice to Poseidon, and all will be well. Tiresias predicted he would die of old age.
Jonathan Burgess, Emeritus professor of Classics, University of Toronto, calls the poem’s ending a “happy” one.

“There’s the recognition that things will follow. Poseidon’s still mad, but in the underworld, Odysseus was told how to stop Poseidon from being angry at him. There’s another adventure coming, but it’s a solution to anger from the divinity Poseidon — something you don’t want to hang over your life,” he says.
What Happens to Odysseus After ‘The Odyssey’?

“The Odyssey” ends with the gods intervening in a suitors’ battle. However, there’s more about Odysseus to be found in “other epics about the Trojan War and what happens after the Trojan War,” Burgess says.

“These existed apparently around the same time as ‘The Iliad’ and ‘The Odyssey.’ Same meter, same kind of poetry, same tradition. They told the whole story, starting from Paris and Helen to the sack of Troy,” Burgess says.
Unlike “The Iliad” and “The Odyssey,” these poems don’t exist in full. Instead, only fragments survived. Proclus, a Roman grammarian, wrote down summaries.
“The cycle poems were valued as context for Homer, but the poems themselves were not valued enough to be sung or to be preserved by the Roman period,” Burgess says.

The epic cycle concludes with “The Telegony,” which is about what happened after Odysseus’ homecoming. Author Madeline Miller looked to “The Telegony” for her popular book “Circe,” about the witch who hosts Odysseus during “The Odyssey.”
“The Telegony” is about Telegonus, the son Odysseus had during his time with Circe. Telegonus is not mentioned in “The Odyssey.”
He goes out in search of his father, carrying weapons from his mom — one being a poison-tipped spear. Eventually, he uses that spear on his father.
“Telegonus has never seen Odysseus. Odysseus has never seen Telegonus. Odysseus assumes he’s some stranger trying to steal his cattle. So they fight, and Telegonus kills his dad,” Burgess says.
Then comes something, perhaps, even stranger. First, Telegonus and Telemachus bring the corpse of Odysseus back to Aeaea, the island of Circe, and bury the body.
“Some people say Circe married Telemachus, and that Telegonus married Penelope. So there’s this strange two new weddings at the end of ‘The Telegony,’” Burgess says.

Burgess says Odysseus also remarries, according to certain myths. After leaving Ithaca to make a sacrifice for Poseidon, he travels to Epirus in northwest Greece. He married Callidice and has a son, Polypoetes, Burgess shares. After Callidice dies, he returns to Ithaca — setting the scene for “The Telegony.”
“The Telegony” place in relation to “The Odyssey” remains a mystery.
“Clearly, ‘The Telegony’ knows of ‘The Odyssey,’ but does ‘The Odyssey’ know of ‘The Telegony’”? Warwick asks.
She thinks “The Telegony” might speak to the idea of tying up loose ends.
“I think it is meant to be a happy ending. This is a way for his family to be happy without him,” Warwick says.

title: Marcello Hernández Goes Off-Script on TODAY, Leaving Al and Sheinelle in Shambles
summary: Marcello Hernández’s impression of Kevin Hart on TODAY left Sheinelle Jones and Al Roker in tears from laughing so much.
story: Hernández plus Hart equals hilarity.

Marcello Hernández and Kevin Hart, who star in the upcoming Netflix comedy “72 Hours,” stopped by TODAY July 20 for an interview that went off the rails when the “Saturday Night Live” star did an impression of the veteran comedian.
Things were already a bit goofy when Sheinelle Jones asked Hernández what it was like working with Hart.
“Do you want to see it? Should I show you?” he replied. “This is what it’s like to work with Kevin Hart.”
Hernández then launched into an impression of Hart on set, telling Sheinelle to pretend to be him asking Hart for advice.
“I’m sorry,” Hernández, fully in character as Hart, said, cutting her off while acting like he was on a phone call.

“They gotta bring the money up!” he said. “Money’s gotta be up if you want me to do that. Listen, I’m good. I’m good, but it’s gonna cost ya! I’m good. I know what I’m doing. Yeah, I’ll be there ... for a price!”
Sheinelle and Hart doubled over in laughter, while the TODAY crew could be heard cackling in the background.
“Add a zero!” Hernández said.
“This is ridiculous,” Hart said in response to the impression.
“No, it’s not,” Hernández fired back, while pointing out that Hart had AirPods behind him.
He joked Hart had the earbuds “just in case a CEO calls and is like, ‘We want Kevin to be the face of Froot Loops.’”
Sheinelle continued to howl, while the camera cut away to Al Roker, who was also doubling over in laughter.
Hernández finally broke character and gushed about Hart.
“I’m grateful to work with Kevin,” he said. “He’s a nice guy.”
Hart returned the kind words.
“I got to witness this in real time. But he is exactly what you would think that he is,” he said, adding that his co-star did “an amazing job” hosting the 2026 ESPY Awards.
Hernández wasn’t quite finished poking fun at Hart, teasing him about his shirt.

“Kevin is waking up in the morning going, ‘Which shirt should I wear? Should I wear a normal shirt, like a human being, or should I put on this weird rust-silver combo? Looks like I’m golfing, but also I’m the maître d’ at a steakhouse,’” he joked.
“Why don’t you ever wear socks? How about we talk about that?” Hart fired back.
“Because I’m Dominican,” Hernández said.
The whole interaction was just too much for Sheinelle.
“I can’t, I can’t,” she said as the interview drew to a close. “I don’t even need to say anything else.”
She then tossed to Al for the weather.
“Add another zero to the temperature,” Al joked, drawing laughs.

title: How to Watch the World Cup Final, Including Closing Ceremony and Halftime Show
summary: The 2026 FIFA World Cup final takes place July 19 between TEAM and TEAM. It will include a star studded closing ceremony and halftime show.
story: The 2026 FIFA World Cup championship takes place July 19 at the New York New Jersey Stadium, better known as MetLife Stadium, in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

The tournament’s final game between reigning champion Argentina and Spain will make history by featuring the first-ever FIFA World Cup Final Halftime Show, an 11-minute extravaganza co-headlined by pop superstars Justin Bieber, Madonna, Shakira and BTS, among others.
For the latest World Cup info, follow TODAY.com’s liveblog
A star-studded closing ceremony will celebrate the tournament’s 48 teams from around the world with performances by Post Malone, Nicole Scherzinger, Robbie Williams, Laura Pausini and IShowSpeed.
Tom Cruise will also make a special appearance during the closing ceremony. EGOT winner Jennifer Hudson will be on hand to perform the United States national anthem just ahead of the game.
Mexico, Canada and the U.S. hosted nearly 100 matches across venues in 16 cities, making the 2026 World Cup the biggest ever.
Read on to learn how to watch the 2026 FIFA World Cup final.
When Does the 2026 World Cup Closing Ceremony Start?

The 2026 World Cup’s closing ceremony now starts at 1:30 p.m. ET on July 19, ahead of the final championship match at New York New Jersey Stadium, also known as MetLife Stadium, in East Rutherford, New Jersey.
The closing ceremony will feature performances by Nicole Scherzinger, Robbie Williams, Laura Pausini and IShowSpeed.
Oscar winner Tom Cruise will also make a special appearance and EGOT winner Jennifer Hudson will sing the U.S. national anthem.
When Does the Match Start?
The 2026 World Cup’s final match kicks off at 3 p.m. ET.
Who Will Perform at the 2026 FIFA World Cup  Final Halftime Show?
This year’s World Cup features the tournament’s first-ever halftime show.
Justin Bieber, Madonna, Shakira and BTS will co-headline the 11-minute show.

title: Xzibit Shares He Still Has The Same Beloved Cat From His ‘Pimp My Ride’ Days
summary: “Pimp My Ride” host Xzibit shared in a social media post on July 16 that Thunder Cat, a cat that he’s had since 2006, is still with him to this very day.
story: Be still our millennial hearts.
Rapper Xzibit shared in a social media post on July 16 that Thunder Cat, a pet that he’s had since 2006, is still with him to this very day.
As many a millennial has pointed out, that means that Xzibit has had his buddy with him since his days, hosting popular MTV show “Pimp My Ride,” which ran from 2004 to 2007.

People were more than impressed with Thunder Cat’s longevity. And with the show centered around turning banged up cars into impressive, often-outrageously upgraded rides, social media users couldn’t help but have a little fun.

“Yo dawg we heard you like cats so we put a litter box and a scratching post in your ‘03 Lincoln Navigator. We call it ‘Navigato’,” one Instagram user commented, mimicking Xzibit’s iconic lines on the show.
Others parodied the show’s theme song.
“🎶 So you wanna be a cool cat? But your kitty ain’t fly? You gotta hit me up because I’m a pretty cool guy ….It’s ya boy X to Z XZibit!” a social media user wrote.
And many others pointed out how Thunder Cat has lived through quite a bit, with one Instagram user writing, “Thunder Cat’s been judging people since MySpace.”

“Pimp My Ride” lasted for six seasons. It cemented the rapper as an iconic MTV television host as he helped hopelessly unskilled drivers turn their vehicles into “pimped out” masterpieces with the experts at auto repair shop West Coast Customs.
The modifications were often just plain wild, as Xzibit would surprise participants with add-ons like a mobile CAT scan machine, a slot machine and a snow cone machine.
Netflix attempted an eight-episode reboot of the show entitled “Resurrected Rides” in 2024. But it was hosted by “SNL” alum Chris Reed rather than Xzibit.
The rapper was so touched by the excitement over Thunder Cat from fans, he posted a follow-up photo on July 18 with the little lady.
“Yall made the last Thunder Cat post go viral,” Xzibit wrote on Instagram. “So she got a battery in her back acting like she ready to have her own s---… 🤦🏽‍♂️”

title: Justin Bieber, Shakira, BTS and More Performing at 2026 World Cup Final Closing Ceremony and Halftime Show
summary: The 2026 FIFA World Cup will continue to make history during the final match between reigning champs Argentina and Spain at New York New Jersey Stadium on July 19.
story: The 2026 FIFA World Cup will continue to make history during the final match between reigning champs Argentina and Spain at New York New Jersey Stadium on July 19.
This year’s World Cup was the first to feature three host countries: Mexico, United States and Canada.

Now, the global soccer tournament is having its first-ever FIFA World Cup Final Halftime Show, featuring star-studded performances. Superstars like Shakira and Madonna, among other big names, will join forces as the co-headliners of the 11-minute halftime show.
For the latest World Cup info, follow TODAY.com’s liveblog
The 2026 World Cup final, which will see Spain take on reigning champions Argentina will also include a closing ceremony designed to honor the tournament’s 48 teams from around the world.
The closing ceremony will also feature special performances from stars like Nicole Scherzinger, Robbie Williams and Jennifer Hudson, among others.
Tom Cruise is set to make a special appearance during the closing ceremony, which begins an hour and a half before the final kickoff.
Read on to learn more about the 2026 World Cup’s closing ceremony and halftime performance.
Who Is Performing During the Closing Ceremony?
The final game of the 2026 FIFA World Cup takes place July 19 at New York New Jersey Stadium, better known as MetLife Stadium, in East Rutherford, New Jersey.
